title: The Last Seat
premise: Write a two-scene theater play, a tense dark comedy in a flood-isolated council chamber. Three rivals discover that the emergency boat has one seat fewer than the public list promised. A signed allocation appears to implicate the person trying to organize the escape. Plant one visible clue in scene one and reinterpret it through a consequential choice in scene two. Connected betrayal, new arrivals or death may occur when earned, but do not force a shock quota. Keep the action performable. A few movable props, doors, lights and offstage sound must carry the production.
pov: Theatre presentation through playable dialogue, silence, stage action and entrances/exits. No prose narrator, no unspoken interior thoughts.
tone_mood: Darkly funny, escalating dread, painfully human stakes.
reader_experience: Subtext, tension and an earned reversal the audience can trace.

style.register: Performable contemporary stage dialogue with distinct tactics.
style.dialogue: Primary dramatic vehicle: contested promises, interruptions and evasions.
style.interiority: Shown through speech, action and silence only.
style.explanation: No novel narration, explanatory recap, or repeated scene opening.

characters.name: Ada
characters.goal: Get her district evacuated without exposing an altered allocation.
characters.voice: Polished public reassurance cracking into terse bargaining.

characters.name: Ben
characters.goal: Secure passage for the people waiting outside.

characters.name: Cyra
characters.goal: Preserve evidence of who changed the passenger list.
characters.voice: Dry literal corrections; silence when pressured.

world_rules: The rescue boat has exactly three seats; the public list names four passengers.
There is no second boat arriving during these two scenes.
No magical solutions, erased deaths, instant travel or shared private knowledge.
All onstage events must be achievable with a desk, four chairs, two doors, papers, lighting and offstage sound.

initial_facts.text: The only rescue boat has three seats, while the public passenger list names four people.
Cyra holds the original allocation paper; Ada holds the public copy.

plot_design.central_question: Who gets left behind when the people controlling the list must answer for it?
causal_dependencies: The missing seat forces a public commitment.
A visible discrepancy changes the next negotiation.
A costly choice reinterprets the clue without resetting the capacity.

world_design.setting: One council chamber, evening; water is rising beyond the doors.

scene_designs.setting: Desk, four chairs, two doors; rising water audible outside
scene_designs.dramatic_function: Force a commitment over the missing seat.
scene_designs.development: Plant a visible discrepancy between the two papers.
scene_designs.restrictions: One scene heading, speaker cues, concise playable stage directions; no prose narration.
scene_designs.choice_and_consequence: Plant a visible discrepancy between the two papers. A material choice changes available options and imposes a cost.

scene_designs.setting: The same chamber with the consequences of scene one still visible
scene_designs.dramatic_function: Force a costly allocation decision under immediate departure pressure.
scene_designs.development: Reveal a causally earned reinterpretation of the planted clue.
scene_designs.restrictions: Continue actual entrances, custody, seat count and commitments. Do not repeat scene one or add unstageable spectacle.
scene_designs.choice_and_consequence: Reveal a causally earned reinterpretation of the planted clue. A material choice changes available options and imposes a cost.
